study_type.nlm: Survey (quantitative survey, serial mediation path analysis)

research_method.claude: Cross-sectional online survey (Qualtrics, Likert-type); Pearson correlations and regression-based serial mediation path analysis with covariates; six hypotheses; DTS (10 items, α = 0.86), VVQ (3 items, α = 0.83), HMU (2 items), single-item PPR
research_method.nlm: Quantitative survey; serial mediation path analysis; six hypotheses; DTS α = 0.86, VVQ α = 0.83, HMU 2 items, single-item PPR
research_method.value: Cross-sectional online survey (Qualtrics, Likert-type items); regression-based serial mediation path analysis (HMU → VVQ → DTS → PPR) controlling for coding experience and time spent coding; six hypotheses; Developer Thriving Scale (10 items, α = 0.86), Visibility and Value Questionnaire (3 items, α = 0.83), Healthy Metrics Use (2 items), single-item perceived productivity rating
research_method.note: Pearson correlations reported by Claude only (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; 12+ industries and organization sizes; 1,282 full-time individual-contributor developers recruited by snowball sampling (social media, Pluralsight platforms)
context.nlm: Industry; 12+ industries, company sizes 1 to 10,000+; 1,282 full-time individual-contributor developers
context.value: industry; developers from 12+ industries (Technology 19.4%, Financial services 11.9%, others) and organization sizes from 1 to 10,000+ employees, recruited by snowball sampling; 1,282 full-time individual-contributor developers
context.note: Snowball recruitment stated by Claude (NotebookLM mentions it under limitations).

space_applied.note: SPACE only referenced (criticized for lacking psychometric evidence for satisfaction/well-being).

cat_productivity.note: Both tag the outcome as Productivity, but it is a single-item self-reported perceived productivity rating (PPR); perceived productivity goes to cat_survey per the definitions.

cat_quality.note: Technical debt only mentioned as a measurement pitfall.

cat_collaboration.note: Both tag the VVQ (work visible and valued by teammates and managers) as Collaboration; DTS also covers knowledge sharing (learning culture) and team support.

cat_satisfaction.note: Developer Thriving Scale (motivation, belonging, support) framed as a driver of developer satisfaction/well-being.

cat_activity.note: Lines of code discussed only as a surface-metric pitfall.

cat_devex.note: Both use 'DevEx' tags generically; no Noda/Storey/Forsgren DevEx framework.

cat_agile.note: NotebookLM tags Healthy Metrics Use as Process/Organizational, but it is a perception of team metric use, not a process metric.

cat_survey.note: All constructs, including productivity, measured by self-report survey items.

evidence.quote: Across 1,282 full-time developers in 12+ industries, we tested the factors of our framework and found it predictive of developers' self-reported productivity.
we conducted a linear regression-based serial mediation path analysis with the HMU as our independent variable, VVQ as our first mediator, DSS as our second mediator, and PPR as our outcome variable
We utilized snowball sampling and advertised our online Qualtrics survey publicly on various social media
evidence.loc: PDF p. 5 (Survey Sample Recruitment and Description)

evidence.quote: To operationalize this complex concept, we also chose to ask developers to rate their own productivity over a recent period of time.
asks respondents to rate the extent to which they believe their technical work is visible and valued by teammates and managers.

Learning culture A developer is 1. learning new skills as a developer 2. able to share the things they learn at work. Support and belonging A developer 1. is supported to grow, learn, and make mistakes by their team
The framework builds on the known connection between developer satisfaction and productivity to answer what drives satisfaction in the first place.
The measure draws from models of thriving in health and psychology to identify four primary factors: motivation and self-efficacy, support and belonging, learning culture, and agency.
